task_brief: This is day 12 of "Art and Music Around Us". That is unit 5 in grade 3. Today is a correction and reflection about giving kind and specific feedback. It takes about 40–60 minutes. It is one day's work, not the whole unit project. Your unit is working toward this: Create a small collection connecting a personal experience to one visual and one musical example. Today helps by working on giving kind and specific feedback. Your unit also covers art and music in daily life, community traditions, respectful listening to new music, and respectful looking at new art. Today adds real evidence toward your unit project.
primary_task: Go back to your earlier work on giving kind and specific feedback and improve it. Do not just replace it. Make a fix-it list. What was not working? Why do you think that happened? What did you change? How can you tell it is better? Keep the old and new side by side. Then look at all the problems together. What do they have in common? Name one thing you will do differently. Honest notes about weak work score full marks here. Keep today's work tied to your unit. Today is about giving kind and specific feedback. It is part of "Art and Music Around Us". Later days in this unit cover other things, like art and music in daily life. Before you stop, do this check: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about giving kind and specific feedback; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. In grade 3 you need one clear try with a grown-up nearby. Say or write your reason in a sentence or two. Drawings, objects, or spoken answers are all fine.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.

task_accessibility_provisions: You can take a break, stretch, or come back to this later. That does not lower your score.

remediation: Reteaching for giving kind and specific feedback follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for giving kind and specific feedback, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for giving kind and specific feedback works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of giving kind and specific feedback, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking giving kind and specific feedback mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply giving kind and specific feedback under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on giving kind and specific feedback rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
